findings.description: The bucket omits any ACL/public access block and is explicitly documented as public, allowing anonymous read (and potentially write) access to objects such as customer-master.xlsx. No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined to prevent public ACLs or policies.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so sensitive customer data stored in the bucket is not encrypted with SSE-KMS or a customer-managed key.
The bucket has no logging block, so access to the (public) data bucket is not audited, preventing detection of unauthorised access.
Versioning is disabled, so objects overwritten or deleted (maliciously or accidentally) cannot be recovered, weakening integrity protection for the data bucket.
A file named customer-master.xlsx containing apparent customer master data is uploaded to the unencrypted, publicly accessible aws_s3_bucket.data, exposing sensitive data to the internet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so financial data is stored unencrypted at rest rather than under a customer-managed KMS key.
The financials bucket defines no logging block, so no audit trail exists for reads or writes of financial data.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so a future ACL or bucket policy could expose financial data publicly without any account-level guardrail.
Versioning is not enabled, so deleted or tampered financial objects cannot be restored, weakening data integrity guarantees.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving operations data unencrypted at rest.
The operations bucket has no logging block, so object access is not recorded for audit or incident investigation.
No public access block is configured for this bucket, leaving no guardrail against ACLs or policies that grant public access.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its contents are stored without SSE-KMS encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or bucket policies for this bucket.
The central logs bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or access to audit logs is not itself audited.
The log bucket has no public access block, so a misapplied ACL or policy could expose collected access logs publicly.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached to any bucket in this file, so plaintext HTTP access to S3 objects is permitted.
